'''Noor Muhammad Butt''' ([[Urdu]]: نور محمد بٹ); b. 3 June 1936), {{small| [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz|SI]], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]}}, also known as '''N. M. Butt''', is a Pakistani [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and professor of physics at the [[Preston University (Pakistan)|Preston University]] who is known for his research publications in understanding the [[Gamma-ray burst|gamma-rays burst]], [[Mössbauer effect]], diffraction, later the [[nanotechnology]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paspk.org/fellow2.htm | title=Profile of Noor Muhammad Butt (scroll down to read his profile)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121085357/http://www.paspk.org/fellow2.htm |website=Pakistan Academy of Sciences website|date=26 October 2006|archive-date=21 November 2008|access-date=19 December 2020}}</ref>

Besides teaching courses in topics involving the [[modern physics]], his career has spent working in branches of physics at the [[PINSTECH|national laboratory]] in [[Nilore]] and has authored several college textbooks in physics based on his research, and presently serving as the chairman of the Institute of Nano Science and Technology at the Preston University.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt">{{cite web |title=Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt |url=https://www.paspk.org/fellow-profile/?fellowID=28 |website=www.paspk.org |accessdate=31 May 2020 |archive-date=24 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924051622/https://www.paspk.org/fellow-profile/?fellowID=28 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Biography==

Butt was born in [[Sialkot]], [[Punjab (British India)|Punjab]], [[British Indian Empire|British India]] on 3 June 1936.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt"/> He is of [[Kashmiris of Punjab|Kashmiri]] descent. He completed his [[Matriculation in India|matriculation]] from the Muslim High School, Sialkot.<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/><ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" /> In 1951, Butt enrolled to attend the [[Government Murray College Sialkot|Murray College]] to study [[physics]] and graduated with [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in physics in 1955, standing top in his class of 1955 of the Murray College.{{rp|3–4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/><ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" />

He went to attend the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] in [[Lahore]] to study physics under Dr. [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|Rafi Muhammad]] where his research was focused towards the [[Nuclear reaction|quantum reaction]] in [[nuclear physics]], covering the topic of bombardment of [[Lithium-6|Li<sup>6</sup>]] high-energy protons to emit the energy spectrum of [[alpha particle]].<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info"/>{{rp|4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/> In 1957, he graduated with [[Master of Science|MSc]] in nuclear physics after successfully defending his thesis written under dr. [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|Rafi Muhammad]].<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info">{{cite web |last1=Butt |first1=NM |title=NUCLEAR RADIATION EDUCATION AND NUCLEAR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY IN PAKISTAN |url=http://urbanpk.com/pakdef/nuclear%26missile/memorial_munirahmed.html |website=urbanpk.com |publisher=Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info |accessdate=7 June 2020 |archive-date=7 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607230942/http://urbanpk.com/pakdef/nuclear%26missile/memorial_munirahmed.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> His graduation was noted in the local university press when he was conferred with the [[Honor Roll|Roll of Honor]] by the university.{{rp|4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/><ref>{{cite web
  | last =(PSF)
  | first =Pakistan Science Foundation
  | author2 =National Commission on Nano Science and Technology (NCNST).
  | title =Dr. N.M. Butt, S.I
  | website =National Commission on Nano Science and Technology
  | publisher =[[Pakistan Science Foundation]]
  | url =https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:XCazF21pVHEJ:www.psf.gov.pk/home/images/staff/cvchairman.pdf+Dr.+N+M+Butt&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESgF89KkeDO6ooH0Ox1mJMR-4m6yfkZbhHmw0DEDvntsPDWptutfUbKtwOmcr6XA0UjsWhxAfgj6tG2u3O8GdGtkOLEhKFfqC2uIaurGgdNsmS0toz06VqOphE88QHoxXkuklShW&sig=AHIEtbQgW5j_ZQ4quPK0VTez8WVim3W6NA
  | access-date =9 November 2016
  | archive-date =8 March 2016
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160308085622/http://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:XCazF21pVHEJ:www.psf.gov.pk/home/images/staff/cvchairman.pdf+Dr.+N+M+Butt&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESgF89KkeDO6ooH0Ox1mJMR-4m6yfkZbhHmw0DEDvntsPDWptutfUbKtwOmcr6XA0UjsWhxAfgj6tG2u3O8GdGtkOLEhKFfqC2uIaurGgdNsmS0toz06VqOphE88QHoxXkuklShW&sig=AHIEtbQgW5j_ZQ4quPK0VTez8WVim3W6NA
  | url-status =live
  }}</ref>

In 1963, he went to attend the [[Birmingham University]] in [[England]] on [[Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan|Commonwealth Scholarship]] for his doctoral studies, and carried out his doctoral studies under Dr. [[Philip Burton Moon]].{{rp|4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV">{{cite web |last1=Butt |first1=NM |title=Dr.N.M.Butt |url=http://preston.edu.pk/pdf_files/N.M.Butt_cv.pdf |accessdate=31 May 2020 |archive-date=21 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621231248/https://preston.edu.pk/pdf_files/N.M.Butt_cv.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> He studied topics in [[Solid state physics|solid state]] physics and [[kinetic theory of solids]] under [[Rudolf Peierls]] while conducting his doctoral studies on the [[Neutron diffraction|diffraction]] with [[Mössbauer effect]] through the [[Mössbauer spectroscopy|spectroscopy]] techniques under Dr. William Burchman.{{rp|17}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Committee |first1=University of Birmingham University Research |title=Research and Publications |date=1965 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TUUPAQAAMAAJ&q=NM+butt+PhD+thesis+Birmingham+university |accessdate=31 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 1965, Butt successfully defended his doctoral thesis and was conferred with the [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in nuclear physics under the supervision of [[Philip Burton Moon]] from the [[Birmingham University]] in [[England]].{{rp|4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/>

He remained associated with the Birmingham University in England and taught various courses on physics as a [[visiting professor]] while he collaborated with British physicist, Dr. D.A. O'Conner, at the Department of Nuclear Physics in Birmingham University.<ref name="cv" /> In 1993, Butt was conferred with the [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] in physics, titled: "''Structure Properties of Cubic Crystals''", that covered wide range of topics in material science and solid-state physics— though this research work was based on independent but [[Classified information in the United Kingdom|authoritative and classified research]] sponsored by the [[British government]].{{rp|3}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV"/>

==Career at Government of Pakistan==
===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission===
{{See also|Neutron bomb}}
[[File:Beta-minus Decay.svg|thumb|right|200px|{{small|The emission of electron and proton from neutron known as [[Beta-minus decay|β-minus decay]] in nuclear physics.}}]]
In 1961, Butt secured employment in the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) as a scientific officer, and worked on the problems involved in [[Nuclear reactor physics|reactor physics]] before departing to England for his doctoral studies.{{rp|6}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> Upon returning in 1966, Butt joined the [[Fast neutron|Fast Neutron]] Physics Group at the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] in [[Nilore]], where he conducted work on the [[neutron diffraction]] to understand crystalline arrangement in the atomic structure.{{rp|2–3}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" />

His career is mostly spent at the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology, the country national laboratory site in [[Nilore]], where he was instrumental in conducting scientific investigations in [[Solid state physics|solid-state]] materials using the [[Lattice dynamical system|lattice dynamical]] settings and [[powder diffraction]] techniques.<ref name="IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt"/> Much of his scientific work at the national laboratory site [[Classified information|remains classified]] in regards to its relation to the development of his nation's [[nuclear weapons]].{{rp|11}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, F Khan. 2012"/> From 1966 to 1978, Butt engaged in further scientific understanding of the [[neutron]], an important [[subatomic particle]], and studied the utilization of the [[Pakistan Atomic Research Reactor]] with [[Neutron Activation Analysis]].<ref name="IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt">{{cite web |title=IAS » Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt |url=http://www.iasworld.org/prof-noor-mohammed-butt/ |website=www.iasworld.org |publisher=IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt |accessdate=5 June 2020 |archive-date=5 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605040705/http://www.iasworld.org/prof-noor-mohammed-butt/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1978, Butt passed over his work in understanding neutron applications when he was appointed director of Nuclear Physics Division where he became interested in the [[nuclear binding energy]] in the nucleus, the isotopic [[island of stability]], [[phonon]] and the [[Mössbauer effect]].<ref name="IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt"/>

While leading the Nuclear Physics Division, Butt oversaw the establishment of the "[[Pakistan Research Reactor#The New Labs|New Labs]]" where many of his contributions were vital in scientific understanding in [[synthetic element]]s such as [[plutonium]] <sup>93</sup>Pu.{{rp|10;410}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, F Khan. 2012">{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Feroz |title=Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistani Bomb |date=2012 |publisher=Stanford University Press |isbn=978-0-8047-8480-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC&q=nm%20butt%20%20 |accessdate=5 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 1984, Butt was appointed as associate director of the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology, and promoted to its director in 1991.<ref name="IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt"/> In 1995, he eventually took over the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology as its director-general, but left the directorship for a chief scientist position in 1996.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" />

In 1998, Butt was part of a small team that eye-witnessed the [[nuclear chain reaction]] during the atomic tests in the mountains of [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]] in Pakistan.{{rp|47}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cheema |first1=Pervaiz Iqbal |last2=Bokhari |first2=Imtiaz H. |authorlink1=Pervaiz Iqbal Cheema |title=Arms Race and Nuclear Developments in South Asia |date=2004 |publisher=Islamabad Policy Research Institute |isbn=978-969-8721-07-7 |pages=237 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZrkhAQAAIAAJ&q=nm+butt+nuclear+weapons |language=en}}</ref> In 1999, he was of the opinion to favor the development of the less destructive [[neutron bomb]] as opposed to the much larger [[blast radius]] guaranteed by the [[Teller Ulam Design|hydrogen-based design]] of nuclear weapons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scientist: Pakistan Can Build Neutron Bomb |url=https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/44212/Scientist-Pakistan-Can-Build-Neutron-Bomb |accessdate=5 June 2020 |work=Tehran Times |date=18 August 1999 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1999, Butt eventually left the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology when he retired as first "[[Emeritus professor|Scientist Emeritus]]", and subsequently returned to academia to teach courses on physics.<ref name="IAS Prof. Noor Mohammed Butt"/>

===Academia and publications ===
In 1957, Butt joined the faculty of physics at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]], eventually becoming the [[Professor|lecturer]] in physics in 1958 and remained at his alma mater till 1961.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" /> He then taught physics at the [[University of Birmingham]] for several years and worked closely with British physicist, Dr. D. A. O'Conner, on the applications of [[diffraction]], [[Schrödinger equation|wave mechanics]], and [[neutron scattering]]. Their work was sponsored and supported by the [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] through the [[Office of Scientific and Technical Information|OSTI]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Search for All Records {{!}} OSTI.GOV |url=https://www.osti.gov/search/author:%22Butt,%20N%C2%A0M%22 |website=www.osti.gov |accessdate=6 June 2020}}</ref> Collaboration between Butt and O'Connor established the scientific confirmation of [[Ivar Waller]]'s [[Phonon|Theory of Phonons]] at the [[Bragg diffraction]] peaks using the [[Mössbauer spectroscopy]] from [[Lithium fluoride|LiF]]'s single crystals.{{rp|2}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> Their work has been extensively cited for several decades and printed in several books including those of Cambridge University Press and North Holland Publishers in the [[United Kingdom]].{{rp|2}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> He remained associated with the [[CERN]] in [[Switzerland]] and the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in [[Italy]] where his work on solid-state physics was widely recognized.{{rp|2–4}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" />

In 1973, Butt joined the faculty of natural science at the [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] and briefly taught a course on [[Solid-state physics|solid-state]] physics and taught courses on [[material science]] while supervised one of his student's [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis at the Quaid-i-Azam University.{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> He also served on the examiner board for doctoral and master's thesis programs at the [[Punjab University, Lahore|Punjab University]] and [[Bahauddin Zakariya University]].{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> He taught courses on physics at the Quaid-i-Azam University until 2000 when he joined the [[University of Oxford]] to teach physics.{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" />

In 1973, Butt authored a college textbook, "''Waves and Oscillation''" that covers wide range of topics in [[Physical optics|wave mechanics]], [[Mechanical vibration|sound vibration]], and [[Optics|theory of optics]], which is extensively used by students in physics and mechanical engineering students in Pakistan.{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" /> In 1996, he also authored a policy book, "''CTBT & Its Implications''".{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="Dr.N.M.Butt CV" />

===Public advocacy===
After his retirement from PAEC in 2000, Butt begin public advocacy for the benefits of the [[nanotechnology]] and engaged in providing [[Nanotechnology education|education]] when he was appointed Chairman of National Commission on Nano-Science and Technology (NCNST) in 2003 and led till 2005.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" /><ref>{{cite web|last=IAS |first=Islamic Academy of Sciences |title=Profile:Dr. Noor Muhammad Butt |url=http://www.ias-worldwide.org/profiles/prof15.htm |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081120003131/http://www.ias-worldwide.org/profiles/prof15.htm |archivedate=20 November 2008 |accessdate=19 December 2020}}
</ref> In addition, he also served as the chairman of [[Pakistan Science Foundation]] until 2010 where the PSF initiated several awareness programs on nanotechnology in Pakistan.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Science profile of NM Butt" />

After 1998, Butt effectively countered the [[anti-nuclear movement]] in the country to roll back the country's [[nuclear capability]] by noting in the public that the country would also have to roll back its programs at its national laboratories and cutting-edge research in [[nuclear technology]] as it was being useful in [[Electricity in Pakistan|energy generation]], [[Healthcare in Pakistan|medicines]], agriculture, medical usage of lasers, electronics, supercomputing, nanotechnology, and communication technology.{{rp|27}}<ref>{{cite book |title=The Concept via GoogleBooks|date=2000 |publisher=Raja Afsar Khan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=peJtAAAAMAAJ&q=high%20tech%20research%20 |language=en |accessdate=19 December 2020}}</ref>

In 2010 interview with the [[News channels in Pakistan|news media]], Butt also vehemently dismissed the American concerns about his nation's atomic weapons fall into the hands of terrorists as "farce claim" noting that [[Taliban|they]] would be unable to select sequence targets to launch the missiles since they don't have required scientific education to understand the [[Permissive Action Link|locking and triggering mechanism]] to activate [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear device]]s.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Tellis |first1=Ashley J. |last2=Denmark |first2=Abraham M. |last3=Tanner |first3=Travis |title=Strategic Asia 2013-14: Asia in the Second Nuclear Age |date=2013 |publisher=NBR |isbn=978-1-939131-28-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YalUAQAAQBAJ&dq=n+m+butt+nuclear+weapons&pg=PA150 |accessdate=6 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref>
